entities.summary:
Baldwin of Alna was a renowned explorer and navigator of the 13th century, instrumental in the Age of Exploration, who played a pivotal role in shaping the maritime trade and cultural exchange between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic regions.

As a key figure in the service of the King of Portugal, Baldwin led several expeditions to West Africa, the Azores, and the Canary Islands, establishing trade routes and mapping the coastlines of the newly discovered lands.

His voyages had a profound impact on the economic and social landscape of the region, as they facilitated the exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures between Europe, Africa, and the Americas.

The legacy of Baldwin of Alna can be seen in the establishment of the Portuguese maritime empire, which would go on to shape the course of world history for centuries to come.

"The sea is my home, and I have spent my life exploring its secrets." - Baldwin of Alna
